summary: San Miguel County ground cabin on Grass Mountain, staffed only now and then from 1914; abandoned by 1931; only debris recorded at the site in May 2013.

facts.design: Ground cabin with no tower: a small frame building with a shingle roof
facts.status_note: Not standing as far as any source describes: old lumber, wire and green glass lay on the ground in May 2013, and the FFLA lists it as gone
facts.agency: Santa Fe National Forest (earlier the Pecos National Forest)

events.note: Telephone line reached the lookout by 1910; Elliot Barker strung it in the summers of 1910 and 1911
Local rancher George Viles rode lookout during a very dry June
Small frame cabin with shingle roof on the summit by 1916; construction date unknown
Ranger Johnson had a telephone installed inside the cabin and staffed it in June
Karl Valentine staffed it for 18 days in July
Listed as an emergency lookout; cabin considered not worth maintaining
Johnson placed watchers there again; the last staffing the history records

The Forest had abandoned it by 1931, though it still served as a patrol point in critical fire weather; the history suggests it may have been closed after 1927. That year Ranger Johnson helped set benchmarks at the site, ran a flagpole up through the cabin roof, and cut down the telephone poles along the line
Still shown as a lookout on maps dated from 1914 to 1936
Seems to still stand in a long-distance 1958 photograph
Old lumber, wire and green glass still on the ground at the site (May 2013); the most recent description found

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The history says Johnson may have closed the lookout after 1927, when tramway linemen took over detection, but also says the Forest had clearly abandoned it by 1931. The story dates the clear abandonment to 1931 and notes the closing may have been earlier.

notes_for_editor: Almost everything comes from one document: the 2017 Santa Fe National Forest lookout history (pp. 133-134 of the PDF), which footnotes its own sources. The 1928 date is the last staffing the history records, not a known last use. The 'may have closed it after 1927' and 'clearly abandoned by 1931' statements are the history's own hedges. Record kind 'ground' and county San Miguel match the sources. No record correction proposed. The site's condition after May 2013 and public access are not described in any source read, so the story says so. Photos in the history are credited to their archives but no URLs were found, so none are listed.
